items.title: Minghui grants ASKA Japanese rights to sub-q TED candidate in $440M deal
items.summary: China’s Minghui Pharmaceutical has licensed its late-stage thyroid eye disease candidate to ASKA Pharmaceutical for up to $440 million, granting the Japanese drugmaker exclusive development and commercialization rights in its home country.

items.title: Blackstone Life Sciences teams up with Boston Scientific in $455M heart pump deal
items.summary: Blackstone Life Sciences has penned a $455 million collaboration with Boston Scientific to co-fund the development of the medtech’s next-generation miniature heart pump system.

items.title: Boehringer returns to Sino Biopharma in $7.4B deal for preclinical TCEs, ADCs
items.summary: Boehringer Ingelheim has returned to China to satisfy its appetite for antibody-drug conjugates and T-cell engagers.

items.title: nPhase rakes in $30M to expand AI-native clinical data platform
items.summary: Clinical research company nPhase has closed a $30 million series D financing round to expand its AI-native clinical data platform.

items.title: AbbVie pens $1.4B deal for deprioritized IBD drug from Nxera
items.summary: AbbVie has added another angle to its relationship with Nxera, with the Big Pharma paying $100 million upfront for a phase 1 inflammatory bowel disease candidate.

items.title: Ultragenyx shrinks workforce and axes assets to halve R&D spend
items.summary: Ultragenyx is laying off 20% of its workforce and axing drug development programs to cut its annual R&D budget to half of the amount it spent in 2025.

items.title: Sanofi scraps STAT6 degrader from Nurix just 2 months after entering clinic
items.summary: Sanofi has decided to end work on a STAT6 degrader from Nurix just two months after taking the inflammatory disease drug into the clinic.

items.title: Novo’s CEO still looking for deals to ‘close some of the gaps,’ as misfires hit profits
items.summary: Novo’s CEO has told Fierce that the company remains on the hunt for deals that “close some of the gaps” in its pipeline, as the Big Pharma reports billions of dollars in impairment charges from a string of recent clinical misses.

items.title: Servier’s $1.6B muscular dystrophy bet on Edgewise delivers quick-fire pivotal failure
items.summary: Servier’s decision to bet $1.55 billion on Edgewise Therapeutics’ muscular dystrophy program ahead of pivotal data has backfired. Five months after striking the deal, the French drugmaker has reported that a Becker muscular dystrophy trial missed its primary and secondary endpoints.

items.title: AbbVie invests £120M in UK, including expanded R&D site
items.summary: AbbVie is investing 120 million pounds ($160 million) to expand its U.K. R&D presence, in a show of faith in the country’s life sciences sector.

items.title: Insulin pump maker MiniMed names David Segal chief medical officer
items.summary: MiniMed has hired David Segal, M.D., as its new chief medical officer, bringing in a diabetes care and digital health veteran as the company enters its next chapter as an independent business.

items.title: Philips sets aside $322M for proposed DOJ settlement over sleep apnea device recall
items.summary: Philips’ Respironics division has reached an “agreement in principle” with the U.S. Department of Justice to settle a long-running investigation into its recall of potentially defective sleep apnea devices.

items.title: Rhythm doubles down on LG obesity license, raising payout to as much as $855M
items.summary: Rhythm Pharmaceuticals and LG Chem have rewritten the terms of their licensing agreement for the oral obesity and hyperphagia drug bivamelagon, growing to $855 million in scheduled payments from the earlier milestone-based deal of $305 million.

items.title: AbbVie abandons phase 2 solid tumor drug over ‘limited benefit’
items.summary: AbbVie has scrapped a phase 2 solid tumor drug after deciding that the monoclonal antibody was unlikely to best the current standard of care, Fierce has learned.

items.title: Pfizer pares back obesity pipeline, drops phase 2-stage lung disease candidate
items.summary: Pfizer has axed a phase 2 pulmonary arterial hypertension program on business grounds, dealing a setback to a long-running effort to treat the lung disease by targeting BMP9.

items.title: Abbott's Tectonic test looks to shift artery disease treatment with ‘early’ win
items.summary: Abbott has posted positive 30-day results from its Tectonic trial of the investigational SonicForce Coronary IVL System in coronary artery disease (CAD), but analysts urge caution on results.

items.title: BioArctic left out in the cold as Novartis walks away from $800M neuro collab
items.summary: Just 14 months after Novartis signed an $800 million biobucks neuroscience partnership with BioArctic, the Swiss pharma has walked away from the deal.

items.title: GE HealthCare debuts ceiling-mounted AI image guidance system
items.summary: GE HealthCare has debuted Allia Celeo, a ceiling-mounted image guiding system, at the Transcatheter Cardiovascular Therapeutics (TCT) 2026 conference.

items.title: FDA grants uniQure’s Huntington’s gene therapy priority review, teeing up ‘defining milestone’
items.summary: The FDA has accepted uniQure’s priority review and application for its gene therapy treatment for Huntington’s disease.

items.title: Alnylam seeks new commercial leader as Tolga Tanguler exits amid faltering Amvuttra trajectory
items.summary: Alnylam Pharmaceuticals is seeking a new chief commercial officer as the biopharma announced that its six-year CCO veteran Tolga Tanguler is leaving the company.

items.title: Sanofi runs emotive RSV campaign zeroing in on a baby’s bronchiolitis breathing sounds
items.summary: Would you know the difference between a normal cold and one that has turned into something more serious? Sanofi is raising awareness of bronchiolitis, a potential complication of RSV in young children, with a new a tough-to-watch PSA video.

items.title: Samsung Bio union vows strike as labor negotiations stall
items.summary: Samsung Biologics' labor negotiations have stalled out amid mounting tension between union members and management. In response, the union says 400 employees will strike starting November 6.

items.title: BMS Canada teams with TANK Worldwide, Ogilvy Health to turn autumn leaves into melanoma awareness campaign
items.summary: Bristol Myers Squibb Canada is partnering with TANK Worldwide and Ogilvy Health on a new “What Summer Leaves Behind” skin cancer awareness campaign.

items.title: Rising Stars: Publicis Health’s Ariel Rabinowitz knows what it takes to 'meet people where they are'
items.summary: Publicis Health’s Ariel Rabinowitz learned lessons about health literacy, trust and access firsthand while teaching at a school in the Bronx.

items.title: Madrigal’s Rezdiffra storms past blockbuster milestone as CEO hails ‘accelerating’ MASH market
items.summary: To Madrigal CEO Bill Sibold, “it’s hard to find a more attractive growth opportunity in biotech” than MASH, as the company’s Rezdiffra, the first FDA-approved MASH therapy, crossed the $1 billion mark in annual sales.

items.title: Amgen's quality chief to retire as internal successor steps up
items.summary: Jackie Elbonne, Ph.D., announced her retirement after 35 years in the biopharma industry, leaving Amgen's chief quality officer role to her deputy, Aine Hanly, Ph.D.

items.title: Pfizer delivers Q3 beat as post-COVID comeback gains momentum
items.summary: Pfizer's third-quarter performance bested Wall Street estimates thanks to an Eliquis beat and 37% growth from acquired products.

items.title: As Bayer spots pharma recovery, questions resurface over potential crop science split
items.summary: Bayer’s pharmaceutical business may finally be entering a long-awaited growth cycle, but CEO Bill Anderson still can’t quite escape the lingering questions around a potential crop science split.

items.title: Lonza bets big on US growth, snaps up Merck KGaA’s CDMO business
items.summary: Lonza will purchase the German Merck’s U.S.-based CDMO network for mid-triple-digit million euros. Besides five sites, the deal will bolster Lonza’s prowess in rapidly growing sectors such as cell and gene therapy, bioconjugates, viral vectors and advanced drug-delivery technologies.

items.title: Sumitomo's Gemtesa power couple takes the wheel in road-trip themed overactive bladder awareness push
items.summary: Actress Holly Robinson Peete and her husband, former professional quarterback Rodney Peete, are hitting the road for another starring role in Sumitomo Pharma America’s Gemtesa campaign, “Time To Go.”

items.title: Hansoh hit with FDA write-up after inspection
items.summary: In a recently disclosed report, the FDA outlined manufacturing concerns at a facility run by China's Hansoh Pharma, with sterilization issues among the agency's chief complaints.

items.title: Inovio’s DNA-based immunotherapy Voceryq approved by FDA for rare HPV airway disease
items.summary: After an initial FDA scare that threatened its path for an accelerated approval, Inovio’s Voceryq, the first plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy, has earned a go-ahead to treat a rare HPV-driven disease.

items.title: Karyopharm files Chapter 11, lines up Ayrmid as lead bidder in planned merger
items.summary: In an answer to Karyopharm's cash crisis, Irish biotech Ayrmid has agreed to make the first bid on the struggling biopharma's assets in a court supervised auction, teeing up a potential hematology merger.

items.title: Compass points to unmet need in depression as landmark psychedelic nears market
items.summary: Compass Pathways has published survey data showing how treatment-resistant depression affects patients and their caregivers, laying the groundwork for the launch of its psychedelic therapy.

items.title: Dexcom taps celebrities, influencers for ‘A Letter to Diabetes’ campaign
items.summary: Dexcom is marking National Diabetes Awareness Month and World Diabetes Day in November with a new campaign asking people affected by diabetes to write a letter to the condition.

items.title: Fresenius strikes WuXi Bio biosimilars deal for up to 37 assets, targeting €370B market
items.summary: Fresenius has inked a broad deal with WuXi Biologics to scale its biosimilars portfolio to as many as 66 molecules targeting a combined originator market worth over 370 billion euros ($415 billion).

items.title: How AI turns field conversations into actionable insights
items.summary: See how STEM AI turns real-world HCP conversations into personalized coaching, strategic insights and stronger field execution.

items.title: HCPs Aren’t Ignoring Your Science. They’re Ignoring How (and When) You Deliver It
items.summary: Make your congress investment work harder. Discover how the right format can deliver 180% more engaged sessions.

items.title: How advanced AI can improve clinical trial decision-making
items.summary: Life science foundation models can help teams anticipate patient outcomes and pressure-test trial designs.

items.title: Proof Over Promise: What a DTP Program Actually Looks Like When It's Working
items.summary: The DTP space is full of providers making bold claims. But claims aren’t outcomes. Find out what a high-performing DTP program actually delivers.

items.title: Sanofi tips Dupixent to reap most rewards from Eli Lilly’s Ebglyss ad push
items.summary: Sanofi has predicted that Dupixent will receive “the majority of the benefit” from the direct-to-consumer marketing campaigns that Eli Lilly is running to support its rival drug Ebglyss.
